description: Hook Master playbook — merged from reference sources (CPD-1086)

psychology.text: Stop the scroll in 3 seconds — one question in the viewer's mind with a promised payoff
Pattern interrupt triggers orienting response — brain notices movement, intense emotion, sudden contrast
Curiosity loop / information gap — text teases without resolving; viewer needs completion
Loss aversion — tease a mistake, secret, or costly miss; FOMO on the reveal
Mute-first: >60% watch without sound — burned text must carry subtext alone
Instant clarity — dense staccato words; specific numbers or objects build trust fast
Hooks must grab attention within the first three seconds.
Create an information gap or unresolved tension.
Use unexpected or contradictory statements to break scrolling.
Design text hooks for mute-first viewing.

formulas.name: Contrarian Hook
formulas.template: I did X, but Y happened.
examples: I made more money after I stopped posting daily
This editing mistake actually increased my views by 300%

formulas.name: Direct Promise
examples: This 5-second edit doubled my watch time.
I'm about to show you why everyone's doing captions wrong.
Watch me turn this disaster into my best video

formulas.name: Question Hook
examples: Why do your Shorts die at 40% watch time?
Ever wonder why big creators never show their full process?
What if I told you captions are hurting your retention?

anti_patterns: Pure Chaos / Intense Face / Sudden Roar without a concrete noun
Mood-only template hooks that fit any clip
Copying Twitch clip title or streamer prefix
Spoiling the punchline or full joke in the hook
Wildest Moments / You Won't Believe / Chat Goes Wild filler
twitch_comp_adaptations: Burned hook = TEXT layer only — visual interrupt comes from the clip itself; text adds curiosity gap
3–6 words ideal on screen; hard max 12 words / 72 chars
Anchor every hook to one concrete noun from Gemini observation (object, action, quoted detail)
Question marks and contrast words boost scroll-stop when observation supports a twist
Never name the streamer — moment beat only
Twitch clips are often watched mute-first, making burned text hooks essential for initial engagement.
Keep burned captions concise (3-8 words) for quick readability and impact.
Text hooks must create an information gap, trigger curiosity, or promise value instantly to stop the scroll.
Utilize text overlay as a primary hook mechanism, as visual and auditory cues may be missed.
